definition: In mathematics and statistics, random projection is a technique used to reduce the dimensionality of a set of points which lie in Euclidean space.
details: According to theoretical results, random projection preserves distances well, but empirical results are sparse. They have been applied to many natural language tasks under the name random indexing.

explainer.lead: Random projection is a technique used to reduce the dimensionality of a set of points lying in Euclidean space. It matters because theoretical results show it preserves distances well, though empirical results are sparse.

tiers.eli5: Squash a high-dimensional cloud of points onto fewer dimensions using a random angle, and the points still end up roughly as far apart as before.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply it to natural language tasks under the name random indexing; the pitfall is that support rests mainly on theory since empirical results are sparse.
tiers.paperLevel: A dimensionality reduction technique for points in Euclidean space; according to theoretical results it preserves distances well, but empirical results are sparse.

explainer.example: A set of high-dimensional Euclidean points is projected to fewer dimensions, retaining approximate pairwise distances; the same approach appears in language tasks as random indexing.
